23 January – The largest interstellar organosulfur molecule (2.5-cyclohexadiene-1-thione) so far is identified in a molecular cloud about 27,000 light-years from Earth near the Galactic Center.
13 July – Astronomers report the detection of erythrulose, a four-carbon monosaccharide, in the interstellar molecular cloud G+0.693−0.027 near the Galactic Center. The discovery is described as the first detection of a "true sugar" in the interstellar medium, distinguishing it from previously identified sugar-related molecules such as glycolaldehyde.
